instrument.assumedRange: MIDI 36-96 (C2-C7) — verify against captured log; octave-shift feature covers material outside this window
instrument.velocity: fixed 100, not gradable — no dynamics nodes exist anywhere in this tree by design
instrument.channel: all notes on ch 1; hands split by configurable splitPoint (default MIDI 60 / C4)
instrument.sustain: permanently on at the instrument, invisible to MIDI; app plays its own dry sampled piano

fieldNotes.dependsOn: array of {id, why}. Unlock rule (see session-generator.md): child unlocks when every dep is at >=80% node mastery and all `requires` are satisfied.
fieldNotes.masteryThreshold: typed shapes, defined in architecture.md §7: deckFluency | timedRun | legato | articulation | sync | voiceLeading | earDeck | dictation | piece | pedalSync
fieldNotes.sustainSensitive: true = the skill concerns note SEPARATION, which the instrument's permanent sustain hides acoustically. Grading is MIDI-based and unaffected, but the drill MUST present/playback through the app's dry sampled piano so he can hear what the grader hears.
fieldNotes.itemCount: approximate count of distinct schedulable items the node generates; 'generated' = procedurally infinite, scheduled by difficulty tier
fieldNotes.isV1: exercisable by the three V1 drills (inversion trainer, chord-detection HUD, finger legato) and near the current frontier

v1Patch.why: Original V1 set was unreachable: every V1 node sat behind a non-V1 root gate, so the unlock rule left the day-one queue empty.
changes: kt-geography isV1 -> true (root gate for all keyboard-theory V1 nodes; 12 items, calibration only)
pr-pulse-sync isV1 -> true (root gate for all physical V1 nodes; 4 items)
ear-intervals-1 isV1 -> true (ear track must start week one; root, no deps, 6 items)
pr-legato-scales isV1 -> false (depends on kt-scales-group1 / scale-run, out of V1 scope)
kt-geography.masteryThreshold.minRepsPerItem 2 -> 3 (was unsatisfiable against the last-3-reps mastery rule)
v1Patch.note: kt-triads-root keeps drillType 'chord-play'; the inversion-trainer component handles it as inversion index 0. No separate grader.

nodes.name: Keyboard geography
nodes.desc: Find any named note in any octave without hunting. Calibration node — likely already near-mastered; expected to clear in one or two sessions and mostly exists to seed latency baselines.

nodes.name: Root-position triads, all 12 keys
nodes.desc: Major and minor triads from a name prompt, root position, any octave. He already KNOWS these — this node converts knowledge to latency: from derived-by-formula to automatic.

dependsOn.why: chord latency is meaningless if part of it is spent hunting for the root note

nodes.name: Major triad inversions
nodes.desc: Root, 1st, 2nd inversion of every major triad, prompted by symbol (e.g. 'Db/F'). The core V1 target: he can work these out in ~4s; goal is <1.2s.

dependsOn.why: an inversion is a re-stacking of a shape that must itself already be automatic, or latency measures two skills at once

nodes.name: Minor triad inversions
nodes.desc: Same mechanic as major inversions, minor qualities.

dependsOn.why: staggered purely to limit simultaneous new-item load (36+36 at once floods the scheduler), not because minor is intrinsically harder — see orderingUncertainties[0]

nodes.name: Major scales: C G D A E
nodes.desc: The five majors sharing the standard 123-1234 fingering. Hands separate, two octaves. Moves him from 'can derive any major scale' to 'has five memorised in the fingers'.

dependsOn.why: scale fluency assumes instant note location; otherwise wrong-note errors are actually navigation errors

nodes.name: Major scales: F Bb Eb Ab Db
nodes.desc: Flat-key majors with non-standard thumb positions. Hands separate, two octaves.

dependsOn.why: establishes the practice mechanic and tempo habit on friendly fingerings before the flat keys break the thumb pattern

nodes.name: Major scales: B and F#/Gb
nodes.desc: The remaining majors. Completes all 12.

dependsOn.why: sequenced last only because they are rarest in his repertoire targets; mechanically they are easy (mostly black keys fit the hand)

nodes.name: Circle of fifths / key signatures
nodes.desc: Key -> signature and signature -> key, both directions, all 12 majors, answered by playing (tonic + the sharps/flats) so recall stays attached to the keyboard.

dependsOn.why: signatures should abstract scales already under the fingers, so the map has sound and shape attached rather than being rote name-facts — see orderingUncertainties[1]

nodes.name: Minor scales (natural + harmonic)
nodes.desc: All 12 keys, both forms, hands separate. Melodic minor deferred to repertoire need.

dependsOn.why: relative-minor derivation turns 24 signatures into 12 facts; without it every minor key is a fresh memorisation
the scale-practice mechanic and thumb-under habit must already be routine so only the new note content is being learned

nodes.name: Diatonic triads by Roman numeral
nodes.desc: Prompted 'IV in A major' -> play the chord. The bridge from letter-name chord charts to functional harmony, and a prerequisite for everything ear-side.

dependsOn.why: building the chord on a degree requires the key's notes to be instantly available
the chord shapes themselves must be automatic so only the numeral->root mapping is being trained

nodes.name: Seventh chords, root position
nodes.desc: maj7, m7, dom7, m7b5 in all 12 keys.

dependsOn.why: 7ths are triads plus one interval; triad shapes must be automatic first or every 7th is built from scratch

nodes.name: Dominant 7th inversions
nodes.desc: All four positions of every dom7. Dom7 first because it is the highest-frequency 7th in every genre he plays.

dependsOn.why: cannot invert a shape that is not yet automatic in root position
the 3-note inversion mechanic (find the bass, re-stack above) must be reflexive before extending it to 4 notes

nodes.name: Remaining 7th inversions
nodes.desc: maj7, m7, m7b5 in all inversions. Long-tail node; expected to be in rotation for months.

dependsOn.why: prove the 4-note inversion mechanic on the highest-value quality before paying for the long tail

nodes.name: Sus, add and extended chords
nodes.desc: sus2, sus4, 6, add9, 9 in all keys. Pop/chart vocabulary, feeds play-by-ear.

dependsOn.why: 9ths are alterations of 7th shapes; sus/add sit naturally after the 4-note habit exists

nodes.name: Shell voicings
nodes.desc: R-3-7 and R-7-3 shells, LH root + RH guide tones. First voicing concept beyond close position; immediately usable in chart playing.

dependsOn.why: shells are subsets of 7th chords; the full shape must exist before parts of it are extracted

nodes.name: Voice leading between diatonic chords
nodes.desc: Connect I-IV-V-I (and 3 other stock progressions) choosing inversions that minimise motion. Metric is fully MIDI-computable: pair upper voices by pitch order between consecutive chords, sum absolute semitone movement.

dependsOn.why: smooth connection IS choosing the right inversion under time pressure; inversions must be automatic or every change stalls
the material is numeral-prompted progressions; the numeral->chord map must not consume attention

nodes.name: Progressions from Roman numerals
nodes.desc: Six stock progressions (I-V-vi-IV, ii-V-I, I-vi-IV-V, vi-IV-I-V, I-IV-V-I, I-bVII-IV-I) in all keys, voice-led, in time. The transposition engine behind play-by-ear.

dependsOn.why: in-time progression playing collapses without reflexive inversion choice; this node adds tempo pressure to an existing skill
numeral vocabulary source

nodes.name: Open and spread voicings
nodes.desc: Two-hand spread voicings (LH root+fifth or tenth, RH upper structure) within the 61-key window.

dependsOn.why: open voicings extend the shell concept upward; shells supply the guide-tone skeleton
upper structures are inversions of the chord's top notes; choosing them must be automatic

nodes.name: Pulse sync
nodes.desc: Quarter notes on one key locked to the Transport click, 60-120 BPM. Baseline for every timing window in the app.

nodes.name: Subdivisions
nodes.desc: Eighths, triplets, sixteenths on one note, and switching between them mid-stream on cue.

dependsOn.why: subdivisions are divisions of a pulse he can already hold; without a stable quarter the reference disappears

nodes.name: Finger legato: five-finger positions
nodes.desc: Stepwise five-finger patterns, each hand. Trains the release timing sustain has been hiding: note N's note-off must land 10-60ms AFTER note N+1's note-on. Stage progression in notes.

dependsOn.why: overlap targets are only meaningful at a controlled steady tempo; rushing destroys the measurement

nodes.notes: Stages: (1) 60 BPM quarters, band [0,80], inBandShare 0.75 — awareness; (2) 72 BPM quarters, band [10,60], 0.8; (3) 72 BPM eighths, band [10,60], 0.85 = mastery. His captured log shows ~60ms overlaps, i.e. he starts at the smeared edge of the band. Always played/monitored on the dry app piano.

nodes.name: Finger legato: scales (thumb-under)
nodes.desc: Full-scale legato where the thumb crossing is the known failure point. Grader reports thumb-under transitions (fixed scale positions under standard fingering) separately from the rest.

dependsOn.why: release timing must be controlled in a static hand position before adding hand relocation
cannot train connection through material still being decoded note-by-note; the notes must already be automatic

nodes.notes: Assumes standard scale fingerings so thumb-under positions are inferable from note index. This assumption should be surfaced in the UI ('use standard fingering or the thumb metric lies').

nodes.name: Articulation control (staccato/detached)
nodes.desc: Deliberate non-legato: note duration as a fraction of the inter-onset interval. Staccato target duty 0.3-0.5. Same release-timing muscle as legato, opposite direction.

dependsOn.why: articulation is the same release-timing control; train the connected direction first since that is his stated gap

nodes.name: Chart playing, graded
nodes.desc: His existing habit, instrumented: RH chords + LH root an octave lower, from a chart, to a click. The chord-detection HUD grades identity and change placement. Doubles as passive telemetry in free-play mode.

dependsOn.why: change placement is graded against a grid; the grid must be holdable first
the chart vocabulary is the triads; they must be playable without derivation for the timing grade to mean anything

nodes.name: LH accompaniment patterns
nodes.desc: LH root / root-fifth / root-fifth-octave in eighths under sustained RH chords. First real hand-independence step beyond the drone habit.

dependsOn.why: adds LH motion inside a two-hand frame that is already stable; changing both hands' jobs at once fails
the LH patterns are eighth-note figures; the subdivision must exist before it is delegated to the weak hand

nodes.name: Alberti bass
nodes.desc: LH low-high-mid-high figures under RH chords, then RH simple melody. The classical accompaniment gateway.

dependsOn.why: Alberti is a harder LH figure in the same role; the role itself must already be automatic
Alberti figures outline triad inversions; if the shape is being computed the figure cannot flow

nodes.notes: sustainSensitive because at speed, permanent sustain turns Alberti into wash; the dry app piano is the only honest monitor.

nodes.name: Rhythmic hand independence
nodes.desc: Different rhythms per hand on fixed pitches: quarters vs eighths, then syncopated RH over straight LH, then swapped.

dependsOn.why: graduates from 'LH busy, RH static' to genuinely different simultaneous rhythms; the intermediate stage must be solid — see orderingUncertainties[3]

nodes.name: Hands-together scales
nodes.desc: Parallel-motion scales, two octaves, both hands. Lives in the physical track because the new content is coordination, not notes.

dependsOn.why: each hand's legato scale must be independently automatic; hands-together exposes whichever hand still needs attention
note material source; only fingered-and-memorised scales enter this node's item pool

nodes.notes: handOnsetSkewMs = |RH onset - LH onset| for simultaneous pairs, hands split at splitPoint. Fully computable.

nodes.name: Arpeggios: one octave
nodes.desc: Major and minor triad arpeggios, one octave, each hand.

dependsOn.why: arpeggio fingerings live on inversion shapes; a computed shape cannot be arpeggiated in time
arpeggios are legato lines with gaps between fingers; release control must precede the wider spacing

nodes.name: Arpeggios: two octaves + dom7
nodes.desc: Two-octave triad arps with thumb crossings, plus dom7 arpeggios.

dependsOn.why: adds the crossing to an existing pattern rather than introducing both at once
the thumb-under move is the same one trained in scale legato, at wider intervals

nodes.name: Polyrhythm: 3:2 and 4:3
nodes.desc: Two hands, two grids. Graded per hand against its own expected grid — fully computable from onsets.

dependsOn.why: polyrhythm is rhythmic independence at the limit; incommensurate grids fail without solid commensurate ones

nodes.name: Two independent lines
nodes.desc: Two-voice counterpoint etudes (easiest Bach minuet tier). The full hand-independence goal: melody against melody.

dependsOn.why: independent lines require independent rhythms plus independent pitches; rhythm alone is the trainable half to secure first
hands-together stepwise motion is the coordination substrate two-voice pieces are built from

nodes.name: Repertoire I
nodes.desc: First real pieces, chosen to fit 61 keys and no pedal: e.g. Satie Gymnopedie-style texture, easy minuets, Yiruma-tier arrangements. Graded against a reference MIDI score.

dependsOn.why: tier-1 pieces are melody-over-pattern textures; the texture must pre-exist so the piece is assembly, not invention
the melodic lines demand real finger legato; without it the pieces only sound acceptable because sustain is lying
tier-1 LH harmonies use inversions freely; slow inversion recall stalls every bar

nodes.notes: See orderingUncertainties[5] — this may deserve to unlock EARLIER with relaxed thresholds, for motivation.

nodes.name: Repertoire II
nodes.desc: Bach minuets / Anna Magdalena book, easy sonatina movements. True two-voice playing at repertoire stakes.

dependsOn.why: performance habits (starting, recovering from slips, tempo discipline) transfer up from easier pieces
tier-2 is contrapuntal; the etude tier proves the coordination before a whole piece depends on it
tier-2 figuration is arpeggio-based in both hands

nodes.name: Repertoire III (pedal era)
nodes.desc: Early-Romantic tier where the sustain pedal is part of the text (easy Chopin prelude tier). Visible now, locked until a pedal exists.

dependsOn.why: technical floor
these pieces are unplayable honestly without measured pedal technique

nodes.name: Pedal basics
nodes.desc: LOCKED until pedal purchase. Foot up/down on cue, in time; CC64 events graded against beat targets.

dependsOn.why: pedal timing is graded against the same grid as note timing

nodes.name: Syncopated (legato) pedaling
nodes.desc: LOCKED. Pedal lifts AS the new chord sounds and re-catches after: lift within 0-120ms after new-chord onset, re-depress within 200ms.

dependsOn.why: the up-down reflex must exist before it is inverted against the hands
pedal changes follow harmony changes; hearing/knowing where harmony changes is prerequisite

nodes.name: Pedal clarity in textures
nodes.desc: LOCKED. Apply legato pedaling inside real textures (arpeggiated LH, melody RH) without harmonic smear.

dependsOn.why: the isolated change must be reflexive before it runs underneath divided attention

nodes.name: Core intervals, ascending
nodes.desc: M2, m3, M3, P4, P5, P8 melodic ascending. Answer by playing the second note from a given first note. Starts week one.

nodes.name: All intervals, both directions
nodes.desc: All 12 within the octave, ascending and descending.

dependsOn.why: the core six anchor the rest as neighbours ('a bit wider than P4'); starting with all 24 classes produces guessing, not hearing

nodes.name: Harmonic intervals
nodes.desc: Simultaneous intervals — the bridge to hearing chord interiors.

dependsOn.why: harmonic hearing decomposes into melodic hearing plus separation; melodic classes must be secure first

nodes.name: Triad quality: major vs minor
nodes.desc: Block and arpeggiated. Deliberately tiny so it clears fast and feeds progression hearing.

dependsOn.why: quality discrimination rides on hearing the third; m3/M3 must be distinguishable in isolation first

nodes.name: Triad quality: dim, aug, sus
nodes.desc: Remaining triad colours.

dependsOn.why: maj/min is the axis everything else is heard against
dim/aug identification hinges on tritone vs P5 vs m6 hearing

nodes.name: Seventh chord qualities
nodes.desc: maj7 / m7 / dom7 / m7b5 / dim7 by ear.

dependsOn.why: a 7th is heard as triad colour plus top-interval colour; both components must pre-exist

nodes.name: Scale-degree hearing (functional)
nodes.desc: Tonic drone + cadence establishes the key; a note sounds; answer by playing it. Movable-do hearing — the single most important ear node for the play-by-ear goal.

dependsOn.why: needs stable pitch comparison, but degree hearing is functional rather than intervallic — this dep is deliberately minimal, see orderingUncertainties[2]

nodes.name: Short melody playback
nodes.desc: 3-5 note diatonic fragments over an established key; hear, then reproduce on the keyboard. Pitch only — free rhythm.

dependsOn.why: melody playback is degree hearing in sequence; single-degree ID must be reliable before chains of it

nodes.name: Melody playback with rhythm
nodes.desc: 1-2 bar melodies, pitch and rhythm both graded.

dependsOn.why: isolates the new variable: same pitch skill, rhythm added
cannot reproduce a rhythm the hands cannot yet produce on demand; otherwise ear errors and motor errors are indistinguishable

nodes.name: Bass-line / root tracking
nodes.desc: Hear a diatonic progression, play its bass line. The load-bearing skill for hearing chord changes in real songs.

dependsOn.why: roots are heard as degrees of the key, not as absolute pitches
mapping a heard root to 'that's the IV' presumes the degree->chord map already exists cold

nodes.name: Progression ID: pop set
nodes.desc: Identify 4-chord diatonic loops (I-V-vi-IV family) by numeral.

dependsOn.why: progressions are recognised root-motion-first; quality colours it second
maj/min discrimination distinguishes vi from IV when root motion is ambiguous

nodes.name: Progression ID: full diatonic + secondary dominants
nodes.desc: All diatonic functions plus V/x chords.

dependsOn.why: extends a working recognition process to rarer functions
secondary dominants are flagged by dom7 colour on a non-V degree

nodes.name: Play by ear I: sections
nodes.desc: Hear an 8-bar section of a simple real song; reproduce melody (RH) over block chords (LH) — his existing two-hand frame, sourced by ear instead of a chart. THE stated goal, first honest form.

dependsOn.why: the melody half
the harmony half
assembly happens in the practiced two-hand frame so the only new work is the ear work

nodes.name: Play by ear II: full songs, real textures
nodes.desc: Whole songs by ear with patterned LH (from pr-lh-patterns) instead of block chords.

dependsOn.why: scales section skill to song length
the target texture
songs get re-keyed on the fly; numeral fluency is what makes the heard progression portable

nodes.name: Transpose by ear
nodes.desc: Take a song already learned by ear and play it in three other keys without a chart.

dependsOn.why: material source
the new key's signature must be instant or every bar re-derives it

orderingUncertainties.issue: Sequenced after major inversions only to cap new-item load. If major inversions clear fast and he reports boredom, run them in parallel instead.
orderingUncertainties.resolve: If kt-inv-maj-triads reaches 50% mastery within a week, auto-unlock minor early.

orderingUncertainties.issue: Placed after the first scale group so signatures abstract lived scales. The opposite school: teach the circle first as the organising map. Both are defensible.
orderingUncertainties.resolve: If scale-group2/3 acquisition is slow, pull circle-of-fifths earlier — the map may be the missing scaffold.

orderingUncertainties.issue: Functional (degree) vs intervallic ear-training order is genuinely contested. Degree hearing may deserve to start week one alongside intervals-1 with NO dependency.
orderingUncertainties.resolve: If interval accuracy is high but ear-melody-1 stalls, degrees started too late — drop the dependency.

orderingUncertainties.issue: These could swap. Alberti-first trains a fixed figure (easier, less general); rhythm-independence-first is more general but more frustrating.
orderingUncertainties.resolve: Both depend only on pr-lh-patterns in ways that permit parallel unlock; let session data decide which he actually tolerates.

orderingUncertainties.issue: Natural + harmonic introduced together doubles the deck. May be better to ship natural only and gate harmonic behind it.
orderingUncertainties.resolve: If the node's accuracy sits below 80% after two weeks in rotation, split it.

orderingUncertainties.issue: Repertoire gated behind three technique nodes may arrive too late for motivation — and motivation is a first-class constraint for this user. A 'preview' unlock (relaxed thresholds, no mastery credit) at half the dependency mastery might be the right adherence move.
orderingUncertainties.resolve: If sessions/week drops below 4 before rep-tier1 unlocks, add the preview mode.

orderingUncertainties.issue: Hands-together scales do NOT gate rep-tier1 in this tree (tier-1 textures are pattern-based, not parallel-motion). If tier-1 pieces expose hands-sync problems, this edge is missing.
orderingUncertainties.resolve: Watch handOnsetSkew inside rep-tier1 grading; if consistently >40ms, add the edge.
